title: Automated incident playbook and postmortem actions for GPU capacity surges
creator: Maya Chen
description: Create an automated, reproducible playbook and a set of low-latency remediation automations to permanently reduce the blast radius from hosted API GPU capacity exhaustion events. The playbook will combine improved telemetry signals, deterministic admission and shed policies, and orchestrated priming/scale flows so on-call can recover capacity faster and automation can prevent cascading queue buildup.
incident_summary: During a hosted API capacity event on 2026-02-18, several GPU pools experienced sustained allocation pressure leading to long queue build-ups, aggressive throttling of customer traffic, and a 3x increase in P95 latency for generation endpoints. Autoscaler oscillation and slow prewarm behavior amplified the impact for high-QPS tenants. Although fallbacks to lower-capacity model variants were available, they were not triggered consistently due to brittle routing rules. This ticket collects follow-ups and implements permanently deployable mitigations.
root_cause: 1) Autoscaler hysteresis combined with a conservative prewarm window caused reactive scale to lag demand spikes. 2) Admission scoring did not sufficiently penalize long-tail KV-cache-heavy requests, allowing a small percentage of requests to consume disproportionate GPU slots and build queue pressure. 3) Telemetry gaps: pool-level queue-depth signals were sampled too coarsely, delaying detection and automated priming. 4) Routing rules for fallback variants required manual toggles and were not tied to pool health metrics.
decisions: Adopt a two-tier admission policy: fast-path latency-sensitive lanes with strict soft-caps and a secondary throughput lane with looser caps.
Implement deterministic eviction for tenants whose requests exceed KV cache or sequence-length heuristics during surge windows.
Tie fallback routing to pool health metrics (queue depth + SLO breach rate) and enable auto-fallback by default for high-risk pools.
Increase telemetry sample frequency for queue-depth and per-tenant slot usage during Canary window to 1s aggregates for 4 weeks.
Prioritize automation over manual runbooks where recovery can be achieved with safe, reversible actions (e.g., soft-prefill, prioritized priming).
action_items: (Arjun Patel) Implement 1s queue-depth sampling pipeline and dashboard: add SLO-based alert rule; due 2026-03-07; estimate 3
(Sofia Alvarez) Implement deterministic admission weights that penalize high-KV and long-seq requests; due 2026-03-21; estimate 5
(Liam O'Neill) Add auto-fallback routing: link model fallback to pool.health and enable opt-out per-tenant; due 2026-03-14; estimate 3
(Nadia Gupta) Build a safe 'soft-prefill' automation that primes GPUs based on short-term forecast and only if prewarm budget available; due 2026-03-25; estimate 5
(Infra Oncall) Run a staged dry-run of the playbook in staging with traffic replay and document outcomes; due 2026-03-18; estimate 2
(Maya Chen) Draft post-deploy runbook and update on-call run escalation matrix; due 2026-03-10; estimate 1
